findings.title: Crash when Google Meet is selected and there is no destination calendar
findings.body:
`const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when the event has no destination calendar (`handleNewBooking` sets it to `null`; other callers pass `[]`). The next line then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining.

Whenever `evt.location === MeetLocationType` and the organizer or event type has no destination calendar, this throws a TypeError. Before this change, that case fell back to Cal Video. Now `eventManager.create` fails and the booking flow errors out after the booking row already exists.

Fix: use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Video booking references no longer store credentialId
findings.body:
The old code was `credentialId: isCalendarType ? evt.destinationCalendar?.credentialId : result.credentialId`, so video results kept their own credentialId. The new code is `credentialId: isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, which drops it for every video (Zoom, Teams, Daily, etc.) reference.

`handleCancelBooking` only deletes the video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set. As a result, cancelling any new booking leaves orphaned meetings at the video provider. Other code that relies on the video reference's credential is affected the same way.

Fix: keep `result.credentialId` for all result types.

findings.title: Organization slug condition was inverted
findings.body:
The original code was `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })`: the slug is set directly only when team billing is disabled, and with billing on it is stored as `requestedSlug` until payment. The new code is `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which flips this.

- Self-hosted / no-billing instances now create organizations with no slug, which breaks org subdomain routing.
- Billing-enabled instances get the slug immediately and bypass the payment-gated slug assignment.

This change is unrelated to the PR's purpose and looks like an accidental logic flip.

findings.title: Google update/delete fallback to the destination calendar can never match
findings.body:
In both `updateEvent` (line 254-256) and `deleteEvent` (line 315-317), the fallback branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy. It then searches `destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)`, comparing against that same falsy value, so it never matches and always yields `undefined`.

Before this change, the fallback was the event's destination calendar externalId. Consequences for references with a null `externalCalendarId` (legacy bookings, and references created by the new no-credentialId and updateLocation paths):
- `events.update` is called with `calendarId: undefined` and fails, so reschedules and location changes are not reflected.
- `deleteEvent` silently targets `primary`, which returns 404 (resolved as success) when the event lives in a secondary calendar, leaving it undeleted.

findings.title: Google createEvent ignores destination calendars that lack a credentialId
findings.body:
`selectedCalendar` is now found only by `cal.credentialId === credentialId`. `DestinationCalendar.credentialId` is nullable, and `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents` has a dedicated path for destinations without a credentialId. For those, no match is found and the event is inserted into `primary` instead of the user's chosen calendar. Previously `destinationCalendar.externalId` was used regardless.

In the same case, the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` (line 168) receives `calendarId: selectedCalendar`, which is `undefined`. That patch is an un-awaited promise, so it rejects as an unhandled rejection and the Meet link is never written into the description.

Fix: fall back to the matching-integration destination's externalId, and use the same resolved id (including the `primary` fallback) for the patch.

findings.title: Office365 always writes to the main host's calendar id, breaking other collective hosts
findings.body:
`createEvent` takes `event.destinationCalendar[0]`, the main host's calendar, and posts to `/me/calendars/${externalId}/events` using the current credential. With this PR, `EventManager` calls `createEvent` once per host's destination calendar, using each host's own credential.

For any non-main host on Office365, that means requesting the main host's calendar id (which may even be a Google address) with the member's token. The request fails and the member gets no event, which is the exact scenario this PR claims to fix.

The `credentialId` parameter added to the `Calendar` interface is ignored here. The service should select the destination matching its credential.

Lark (`larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` lines 128-129, 164-165) has the same problem.

findings.title: CalDAV hosts other than the main host get no event, yet creation reports success
findings.body:
`createEvent` filters the user's calendars with `c.externalId === mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId`, where that externalId belongs to the first (main host's) destination calendar. When called with another collective host's CalDAV credential, none of that user's calendar URLs match.

`Promise.all([])` resolves, `responses.some(r => !r.ok)` is false, and the method returns a successful result with a uid. The booking reference is stored, but no event exists on the member's calendar, so the failure is silent.

Fix: select the destination calendar that matches this credential (via the credentialId parameter) instead of index 0.

findings.title: Team members' destination calendars dropped when organizer has none
findings.body:
`evt.destinationCalendar` is set to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar (line 1067). The collective merge then does `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which is a no-op on `null`.

In that case every other collective host's destination calendar is silently discarded, and no events are created in their calendars.

Fix: initialise to `[]`, or assign `evt.destinationCalendar = [...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`.

findings.title: updateLocation references lose externalCalendarId and credentialId
findings.body:
`referencesToCreate` in `updateLocation` now uses `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`. Calendar results come from `CalendarManager.updateEvent`, whose return object contains neither field. Before this change, they came from `evt.destinationCalendar`.

New calendar references created by `editLocation.handler` are therefore persisted with null `externalCalendarId` and `credentialId`. On a later cancel this has two effects:
- `handleCancelBooking` takes the legacy path, iterating every organizer calendar credential.
- Google `deleteEvent`, given a null externalCalendarId, targets `primary` (see the dead-fallback issue), so events on secondary calendars are not removed.

findings.title: No-credentialId destination path no longer stores externalCalendarId on references
findings.body:
For destination calendars without a credentialId, `createEvent(c, event)` is called without the `externalId` argument. The resulting reference (line 169, `result.externalId`) is stored with `externalCalendarId` undefined, whereas previously it was `evt.destinationCalendar.externalId`.

Later updates and deletes for these bookings then hit the Google null-externalCalendarId paths, which now fail (update) or target `primary` (delete).

Fix: pass `destination.externalId` here as well.

findings.title: Webhook payload shape of destinationCalendar changes from object to array/null inconsistently
findings.body:
`CalendarEvent` is spread directly into webhook payloads (`sendPayload(..., {...evt, ...})`). Changing `destinationCalendar` from a single object to `DestinationCalendar[]` silently breaks existing webhook subscribers, Zapier templates and payload templates that read `destinationCalendar.externalId` or `.integration`.

The value is also inconsistent across paths, as the updated e2e expectations show:
- `handleNewBooking` sends `null` when empty.
- confirm, cancel and payment handlers send `[]`.

This external contract change is not documented, and a single representation should be used.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation repeats deletes per reference and never deletes other hosts' events
findings.body:
The recurring branch (organizer credentials × all updated bookings) now sits inside a `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` loop. For a collective booking with N calendar references, the same set of delete calls is issued N times.

The inner logic still uses only `updBooking.references.find(ref => ref.type.includes("_calendar"))`, the first reference, and only the organizer's credentials. Team members' events for the remaining occurrences are never deleted, leaving orphaned events in their calendars.

findings.title: updateAllCalendarEvents error is now silently swallowed
findings.body:
The catch block still builds a descriptive `message`, but the `console.error(message)` call was removed. Any failure, such as a missing credential causing `updateEvent(undefined, ...)` to throw, now returns `success: false` results with no log at all. That makes reschedule and location-update failures very hard to diagnose.

Fix: restore the logging, using the module logger.

findings.title: loadUsers refactor drops organization select and turns client errors into 500s
findings.body:
Two unrelated changes were bundled into this refactor:

1. The dynamic-user query no longer selects `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`. Any downstream use of `user.organization` for dynamic group bookings, such as building org booker URLs, now sees undefined.
2. An empty or invalid `dynamicUserList` now throws a plain `Error` (line 728). The catch block maps any non-HttpError to `HttpError 500 "Unable to load users"`, so malformed client input becomes a server error.

Separately, the `!Array.isArray(hosts)` check after `|| []` is dead code.
